decisions_log.notes: THE SIZE QUESTION WAS CONVERTED FROM TASTE TO MEASUREMENT BEFORE BEING ASKED. Rather than bring the operator a byte-count argument, the qa lane executed its arms harness against THREE variants plus a reference floor, which dissolved the framing I had been about to present: 'accept 2.07x or lose a corpus member' was a FALSE DILEMMA, because V-TRIM-1 holds 6/6 positive and 0/6 false-positive at 82% of the bytes. Table: V-FULL 5015 B / 2.07x / 6/6 / 0/6; V-TRIM-1 4127 B / 1.70x / 6/6 / 0/6; V-TRIM-2 3989 B / 1.64x / 5/6 RED (loses V-5 AT-193b); V-CORE floor 1936 B / 0.80x / 5/6. C-39 re-derived independently at 2427 B. V-TRIM-2 was disqualified on EXECUTED grounds rather than deference: its instances scan 0 hits across 14 stack terms, so relocating them to docs/engineering-rules.md would invert the project's own placement rule (which sends STACK-SPECIFIC content there), reverse the operator's absorption ruling and falsify three derived requirements, for 138 B. THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR MORE DETAIL BEFORE RULING, AND THAT REQUEST CHANGED MY RECOMMENDATION. I had recommended the hybrid (4491 B, 1.85x, keeps the worked example). Decomposing the (Origin: ...) sentence by sentence to answer the question showed each of the six does a DISTINCT job: S1-S2 why the rule exists; S3 the AT-172b worked example, live on main, the only encoded proof C-40 catches what C-10/C-31/C-39 miss; S4 the concrete case behind instance (i) = P-6; S5 the concrete case behind instance (ii) = P-7; S6 the measured 4-of-6 versus 6-of-6 that makes the two-limb structure load-bearing and guards it against a future one-limb 'simplification'. So the hybrid would have cut the evidence for the two instances the operator RULED absorbed, plus the anti-regression measurement. THE DECIDING ARGUMENT, and it is the batch's own thesis turned on itself: C-40's instance (ii) states that a consolidation dropping observables is a defect because 'a green count over the survivors cannot see the casualties' -- and every trim variant still measures 6/6 precisely BECAUSE the arms test the RULE, not the Origin, so the trim's cost is structurally invisible to the measurement. Trimming C-40's evidence base to hit a byte target would be instance (ii) committed on the control that states instance (ii). The counter-argument was put to the operator rather than argued around: +10.7% on a 59260 B file read at every phase of every batch is a real cost, S1-S6 are the most compressible prose in the block, and none of them changes what the rule does today. CONTEXT THAT MATTERS FOR ANY FUTURE RE-LITIGATION: the 1x cap is NOT an external standard -- the qa lane invented it in its own run 1 as the discharge for the orchestrator's Phase-0 risk R-c, in two arms ('<= the length of C-39, OR the discrimination arm justifies the excess explicitly'), so only arm 1 is breached and arm 2 exists for exactly this case; and qa itself self-reported B-2, that arm 1 is NOT like-for-like because it caps a control absorbing THREE candidates against C-39 which carries ONE, and prices narrative evidence identically with rule text. Per absorbed candidate C-40 is ~1.67x C-39, BELOW C-39's density. FOURTH AND FIFTH IN-BATCH INSTANCES OF C-40 CATCHING ITS OWN AUTHORS, both self-reported: the architect's two cost estimates were wrong by 16% and by 2.3x (asserted ~4300 B, measured 5015 B; asserted ~1100 B saving, measured 2538 B), corrected visibly in section 9.1 rather than quietly; and the qa lane found that its OWN run-1 c40_arms.py NEVER OPENS ANY C-40 TEXT, so its 6/6 was invariant under every possible wording of the control -- by C-40 limb 1 the harness that measured C-40 was itself vacuous, there being nowhere to apply the reddening mutation. Its corpus numbers stand (that is what its expression ranged over, each traced to file:line) but it could not have measured a variant, which is why this task needed a NEW harness rather than a re-run; the new one reads each variant's bytes and its anchor-corruption mutation reddens it 6/6 -> 2/6. Together with A-3 (the architect's limb-1 wording resolving 'the subject' to the batch's change, reproducing qa's executed 1/6 false positive against AT-174b) and A-8 (the orchestrator's refuted C-1..C-39 claim) and V-6, that is FIVE times in one batch that the control under encoding caught its own authors. That is the strongest available evidence it is operable, and it is recorded as the postmortem's likely headline.

decisions_log.notes: THE DISCHARGE AUDIT returned DISCHARGED-WITH-FOLDS: 38 source findings enumerated, 31 genuinely closed, 4 properly carried with a reason, 3 NOT closed. It audited against the SOURCE REVIEWS rather than the fold's amendment table -- the same briefing choice that caught fold 1's twenty drops -- and it upheld BOTH of my refutations while catching me being inconsistent about them: I applied the read/write-race correction to U-2 and U-1 but NOT to U-3, which was snapshotted under the identical condition, and U-3(b) is in fact discharged at section 10.2, so only U-3(a) stands. ROOT CAUSE OF THE THREE ITERATIONS, NAMED AT THE CAP AS THE FLOW REQUIRES, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN CARELESSNESS: the acceptance layer has been measuring a MOVING TARGET. Every fold changes the normative text, every arm figure is measured against that text, so each fold silently invalidates the measurements taken against the previous version. The audit proved it mechanically rather than by inference -- AT-B64-04 was executed against the rider's 890 B body while the shipping body is 1975 B, and the prefix guard sits at offset 1241 while the character-list clause sits at 245, DISTINCT SPANS, so the claimed mutation 'delete the character-list clause -> 6/9 losing #5/#7/#9' is IMPOSSIBLE against shipping bytes and #9 is independently carried. THE FIX FOLLOWS FROM THE DIAGNOSIS and is why fold 3 has a different shape from folds 1 and 2: freeze the text first, measure once against the frozen bytes, and make the binding PROVABLE. Fold 3 was instructed to measure NOTHING. It delivered section 3.0 FROZEN PASTE MANIFEST: six paste blocks with destination, byte count and SHA256, plus a concatenation hash, and a normative extraction rule so any party can reproduce the digest rather than trust it. 6219 + 2411 + 4306 + 1540 + 5962 + 7265 = 27703, matching the concatenation's measured length, so no block was dropped or double-counted. Blocks 1-4 were verified byte-identical to fold 2 by EXTRACTING AND HASHING before and after the fold's edits rather than asserted, and the four hashes independently reproduce the audit's prefixes. Section 3 now covers ALL SIX edited files: the two missing paste blocks were the lineage memory and BACKLOG.md, whose absence made D-11's restored obligation undischargeable for an out-of-VCS leg with no PR, CI or diff. The normative clause that matters: A FIGURE IS ADMISSIBLE ONLY IF IT NAMES THE BLOCK HASH IT WAS MEASURED AGAINST. Every arm figure in the spec is now marked STALE pending re-measure, deliberately not deleted and not restated as current. TWO ITEMS THE FOLD REFUSED TO DECIDE, both correctly. Both are the first items of the measurement pass. ARCH BLOCKER-1 IS RE-OPENED, NOT CLOSED: section 4.3's transcript is WITHDRAWN as a discharge and retained only as a record, and the AT-B64-04 re-run against the frozen block 2 with shipping-clause mutations is a BLOCKING Inc-3 gate condition.
